Headteacher's Welcome
I am proud to be the Head Teacher for Woolston Infant School, a happy, friendly, caring and exciting place where every child matters and children come first.
I hope the website gives a true flavour of Woolston Infant School: the well-behaved, inquisitive and hard-working children, the talented, professional and welcoming staff, the supportive and interested governors, and the caring and positive parents and friends of the community who all make this school a special place.
We aim to develop all aspects of children's learning, placing a high priority on their personal and social development as well as high academic success. The curriculum is well planned in an environment that encourages children to become independent, confident and make choices for themselves.

Partnerships
Hamwic Education Trust
Woolston Infant School is part of Hamwic Education Trust - one of the largest multi-academy trusts in the South of England. Its academies work in local community partnerships based in Southampton, Portsmouth, Poole and East Dorset.
Hamwic Education Trust celebrates the uniqueness of pupils, staff and schools, and aims for everyone to achieve their full potential through the pathways of opportunities available.

pageCache.pageTitle: Breakfast and Afterschool Clubs | Woolston Infant School
pageCache.text:
Breakfast and Afterschool Clubs
Breakfast and Afterschool Clubs
We are fortunate enough to have an After School Club and Breakfast Club onsite.
Both our Breakfast Club and After School Club are ‘Ofsted’ registered, run by qualified staff and provide quality care for the children in our school.
Ofsted Registration No: 116110
Rachel Grant
Sarah Catton
Claire Sinclair
Breakfast Club
Our Breakfast Club starts at 8am and the children are taken through to class at 8.35am. The children are offered a healthy breakfast and are engaged in a range of activities. The cost per session is £4.00. You will need to complete a registration form before your child can attend.
Woolston After School Club
After School Club runs from 3.05pm-5.45pm. The children are collected from their classroom or from onsite activity clubs. Cancelled bookings are chargeable unless 24hrs notice is received (this includes Monday sessions).
Both clubs are closed during the school holidays.
To use these facilities you need to enrol your child by completing a registration form which can be obtained from the school office.
Places in Breakfast and After School clubs are limited and therefore cannot be guaranteed.
Once your place is confirmed you can make payments via MCAS and we also accept payment by child care vouchers.
Our Contact Details
Telephone No: 02380 444447 (School)
Mobile No: 07716457710 (WASC Club hours only)
E-mail: info@woolstoninfantschool.co.uk

Music
Curriculum Vision: Music
“Where words fail, music speaks…” - Hans Christian Anderson
At Woolston Infant School every child is a musician. We believe that music is a universal language which has the potential to inspire and foster creativity in all our pupils. Singing assemblies are held to develop children’s voices, as well as to bring pupils together to experience the act of singing together as a collective. A musical calendar has been developed for the school in order to expose children to wide range of artists and music genres. Pupils begin to learn simple songs and changes from the beginning of Reception, with every child given the opportunity to perform to an audience in the school’s nativity. Pupils engage with music critically through weekly music lessons: listening to, reviewing and evaluate music from periods, genres, styles and traditions.
Key artists have been selected to expose pupils to a wide range of highquality music. By the end of Key Stage 1 all pupils will have been able to perform, compose, play tuned and untuned instruments and use their voices expressively and creatively. We recognise the pivotal part that music plays in enabling pupils to increase their confidence, resilience and cultural awareness.

pageCache.pageTitle: After School Activities | Woolston Infant School
pageCache.text:
After School Activities
After School Activities
Our after school activity clubs are run by qualified sports coaches. and are usually available after October half term.
We offer various clubs including football, multi-skills, computing and duplo. These are subject to change.

Art
Curriculum Vision: Art
“Some painters transform the sun into a yellow spot, others transform a yellow spot into the sun.” - Pablo Picasso.
At Woolston Infants School, our purpose in Art is to provide a pathway for creative expression and allow children to develop what Art means to them. We aim to ensure that Art is accessible for all in every lesson and that all children gain the knowledge and skills necessary to experiment, invent and create their own works of art. Our Art and Design curriculum enables children to discover new artists, old and young, and encourages them to be inspired by them. Children follow through a process of designing, making and evaluating their artwork, with additional time to explore and practice new skills before completing final pieces. At Woolston Infant School, Art allows children to develop necessary life skills such as problem-solving and understanding of the world around them, and make links between other areas of the curriculum.
An artist at Woolston Infant school is provided with opportunities to be creative, imaginative, and be inspired. Our vocabulary rich content allows them to develop the knowledge, skills and vocabulary they need to be successful artists.

Computing
Curriculum Vision: Computing
At Woolston Infant School, we aim to deliver a high-quality computing curriculum in order to equip all of our children, whatever their abilities, with the skills, thinking and vocabulary they will need for the ever-changing, technology dominated world in which they are living in.
Our aim is to ensure that all our children leave Woolston Infant School digitally literate with the skills and thinking they need for wider education and life. They will learn the key principles of information and technology, how to safely use and create digital systems through programming, the ever-growing technological world and E-safety. E-safety is at the heart of the computing curriculum and a part of every lesson ensuring that children are prepared with strategies that help them to make confident and safe judgements about their online activity at school and at home.

DT
Curriculum Vision: DT
At Woolston infant school, we aim to develop and nurture children’s creativity and imagination by providing them with memorable, engaging, and purposeful experiences within a variety of contexts. Our Design and Technology curriculum provides children with opportunities to go through the full designing process; from discovering other designer and inventors, generating their own ideas, making new and unique products, and finally evaluating these products. By going through this process, children begin to develop critical understanding of the world around them, and make links between other areas of the curriculum.
A designer at Woolston Infant School is provided with the opportunity to flourish, take risks, become resourceful and innovative. Our vocabulary rich content allows them to develop the knowledge, skills and vocabulary they need to be successful designers and makers.

English
Curriculum Vision: English
Our aim is for all our children to be fluent readers, with a love of literacy, able to communicate effectively – both orally and in writing. We want our children to be knowledgeable across the curriculum, which is adapted according to their needs. Our curriculum has key milestones to make expectations clear. It is well sequenced and planned so that knowledge is built upon, the curriculum is sequential and progressive from Early Years to the end of Year 2. We encourage our children to have high aspirations and to believe in themselves, so that they feel successful at every stage of their education and beyond.
Writing planning should follow our school format and include the following:
A clear independent outcome.
Clear purpose for writing.
National Curriculum taught skills.
Planned, high level vocabulary.
Follow the school’s agreed lesson structure.
Oracy
Communication is the most important skill in life. To understand and be understood is a basic human need which our curriculum has at its heart.
Present ideas clearly.

Geography
Curriculum Vision: Geography
At Woolston Infant School our ambition is for each and every child to develop a curiosity and fascination about the world around them that will remain with them throughout their lifetime. Every child has the opportunity to explore, observe, and find out about people, places, natural and human physical factors – equipping them with the skills necessary to be a geographer. We offer our children a diverse and knowledge rich curriculum which is deeply rooted in the locality of the school and its surrounding areas. Frequent opportunities are provided to observe and record seasonal changes in weather. The curriculum progression will expand outwards from our immediate locality (Woolston) to comparing and contrasting globally – linking to the overarching aim of promoting global citizenship. Children are guided to make sense of the physical world and their community with regular opportunities for fieldwork to embed the key concepts of location and place, mapping and land use.

History
Curriculum Vision: History
At Woolston Infant School we strive for the teaching of history to inspire curiosity about the past both in Britain and beyond. The curriculum content for history is rich in both knowledge and skills. It exposes children to new and relevant vocabulary, develops their understanding of chronology and ordering events and allows children to understand abstract content through becoming familiar with sources and evidence.
Our history curriculum provides ample opportunity for children to ask perceptive questions, begin to think critically, sift arguments, weigh and judge evidence and begin to develop individual perspective. Through the teaching of history, we endeavour to communicate to children the complexity of people’s lives, the process of significant changes, the diversity of contemporary societies and relationships between groups, as well as considering their own identity and challenges in modern times.

Maths
Curriculum Vision: Maths
We intend to provide a Mathematics curriculum that immerses pupils in learning that is memorable, engaging and meaningful. Provide a maths' curriculum which enables pupils to acquire and develop the knowledge, skills and vocabulary they need to be successful mathematicians. Our Maths' curriculum will enable the children to develop, apply and embed their skills through linked learning, building on what they already know and can do. The maths' curriculum enables pupils to acquire and develop a strong understanding of key mathematical concepts which builds on prior learning as they progress through the school. By having a curriculum that provides deeper learning opportunities we shall endeavour to provide the highest standard of education for every child.

PE
Curriculum Vision: PE
We provide a PE curriculum that immerses pupils in learning that is memorable, engaging and meaningful. The PE curriculum enables pupils to acquire and develop the knowledge, skills and vocabulary they need to be successful. Our PE curriculum will enable the children to develop, apply and embed their skills through Real PE units, building on what they already know and can do.
Woolston Infant School is proud to be a real legacy school and is striving to create a new ambition for EVERY child.
Not only are we on a mission to get our children more active by developing the fundamental movement skills that are so often overlooked, our PE lessons are centred around the child to enable them to be successful in the classroom and in later life.
Real legacy allows us to bring the school, home and the community together to enable cultural change. Our journey commenced with real PE teacher training to support our PE provision to develop the whole child and extends across the school to include supporting families and the wider school community. The school is supported with teacher training, school based support, fun real play activities for families, enrichment and competitive opportunities and supporting resources from Create Development all through a holistic approach to also develop children's personal, social and emotional skills

PSHE
Curriculum Vision: PSHE
At Woolston Infant School we aim to enable the social, moral, spiritual and cultural development of children through day to day teaching of aspects of Personal, Social, Health and Economic education in all areas of life of the school.
We cover the three core themes of Health and Wellbeing, Relationships and Living in the Wider World through teaching that has been sensitively and inclusively tailored for each year group as well as through daily wider work of our school e.g. assemblies, our learning about ‘The Golden Rules’, about our school values which encompass the British Values and whole school and year group memorable learning experiences.
With respect to the children’s and parents’ backgrounds and beliefs, we teach them about safeguarding, including the online safety, relationships, as well as the concepts, skills and attitudes needed to enjoy and manage their lives now and in the future. We strive to prepare children for challenges and opportunities of adult life by building their confidence, resilience and empathy, by helping them to identify and manage risks and emotions, to make informed choices and communicate, to work with others and to form and maintain good relationships.

RE
Curriculum Vision: RE
At Woolston Infant School our aim to develop happy, confident and curious learners who are keen to explore the world around them. We set out to develop pupils’ understanding of a range of faiths, views and beliefs both in and beyond our local area. Pupils at Woolston Infant School explore religious beliefs in depth – appreciating the similarities and differences between Christianity and other faiths such as Hinduism. Our Religious Education curriculum provides all children with a strong foundation built on knowledge. This allows our pupils to develop critical thinking skills, and to develop respectful and open-minded attitudes.
We follow Living Difference IV, the agreed syllabus for the teaching of Religious Education in Southampton and Hampshire. Living Difference IV offers a set of principles for teachers to use to ensure that Religious Education is open to the plurality of ways in which people live in our local, national and international communities.
Parents have the right to withdraw their child from any part of the RE curriculum. Please speak to Mr Arthur if there are any concerns.

Science
Curriculum Vision: Science
We provide a Science curriculum which immerses pupils in learning that is memorable, engaging and meaningful. We seek to stimulate children’s curiosity and excitement about Science.
The Science curriculum enables pupils to acquire and develop the knowledge, skills and vocabulary they need to be successful as future scientists.
Our Science curriculum aims for the children to develop, apply and embed the knowledge through interlinked learning, building on what they already know and can do by knowing more and remembering more.
With regard to the context of our children, we aspire to enrich their cultural capital in Science and enable them to enhance their experiences and opportunities available to them. This will help children to build positive, inquisitive attitudes to Science, to better understand the world around them and to prepare for the rapidly changing world of tomorrow.

SEND Information and Local Offer
SEND Information and Local Offer
It is our aim to enable all pupils at Woolston Infant School (including those with special educational needs) to:
Woolston Infant School is a mainstream setting that educates 180 children from the age of 4 to 7. We welcome children of all abilities and needs. Admission of children with Education and Health Care (EHC) plans is supported by the Local Authority in consultation with the school, parents and carers. We firmly believe in inclusion and that all children should be given every opportunity to thrive in our mainstream setting. Physical and sensory difficulties and medical needs, including visual and hearing impairment.
We have high aspirations for our children and are passionate about ensuring that all of our pupils receive a relevant, broad and balanced curriculum through high quality inclusive teaching. This will enable our children to become independent, self-motivated, life-long learners.
We value and nurture creativity and difference in every child and fundamentally believe in a holistic approach to education combining a resolute focus on the core curriculum subjects, along with an expansive topic based curriculum and extracurricular activities. However, we understand that some children will benefit from a differentiated curriculum and additional support in order to reach their full potential.
Our Special Needs Coordinator (SENCO) is Amy Vaux.
All members of staff are responsible for the operation of the Special Needs Policy and the coordination of specific provision made to support individual children with SEND. They liaise with other professionals to ensure that the appropriate provision is in place to meet a child’s needs.
The school environment has been adapted to allow accessibility for wheelchairs.

SEND Provision Complaints
What do I do if I have a complaint about SEN provision?
Complaints about SEN provision in our school should be made to the SENCO, Amy Vaux, in the first instance. They will then be referred to the school’s complaints policy if needed.
The parents of pupils with disabilities have the right to make disability discrimination claims to the first-tier SEND tribunal if they believe that our school has discriminated against their children.
They can make a claim about alleged discrimination regarding:
Exclusions.
Provision of education and associated services.
